result.note: Tests the India–Canada trade talks and the CEPA format; the India–US deal is skipped because it is only expected, not concluded.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about India–Canada trade relations as of October 2026:
items: Bilateral trade between India and Canada rose 8.2% to $7.95 billion in fiscal year 2025-26.
The fifth round of trade negotiations began in October 2026, with a final deal targeted by December 2026.
The diplomatic freeze between the two countries began in 2023 after then-PM Justin Trudeau alleged Indian involvement in the killing of Hardeep Singh Nijjar.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 1 is wrong because bilateral trade fell 8.2% to $7.95 billion, not rose. Canadian Trade Minister Maninder Sidhu was due to visit New Delhi in October 2026 with a 300-strong business delegation, ahead of Prime Minister Modi's planned December visit.
questions.source: Bilateral trade between India and Canada fell 8.2% to $7.95 billion last fiscal year, but momentum is shifting fast.

questions.prompt: In October 2026, India and Canada began the fifth round of talks on which type of trade agreement?
questions.explain: The talks are for the India–Canada Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA), with a final deal targeted by December 2026. TBB reads the speed of these talks as a signal to US negotiators that India has viable alternative export destinations.
questions.source: Fifth-round talks for the India–Canada Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA) kick off today, aiming for a final deal by December.
